# Double Heston 2.0 on NIFTY 50: results report

*Generated by `dh2/report.py` from `results/metrics.json` (1479 numbers, each with its source file and column or key). Nothing in this file is typed by hand. Development period 2016-2021, test period 2022 onward; errors are implied-volatility points. Not investment advice.*

## 1. Headline: next-day forecast error

On the 1173 test days the jump model plus yesterday's misfit has a mean next-day error of 1.034 vol points; the best model-free benchmark (time-scaled smile) has 1.236. The paired difference is -0.202 [-0.227, -0.181] (95% block bootstrap). The model beats the time-scaled smile in 5 of 5 test years (and 6 of 6 development years, where the settings were chosen; 2016 and 2026 are partial years). That benchmark repeats its edge value for strikes yesterday did not quote; against a benchmark that continues the wings linearly the paired difference is -0.045 [-0.061, -0.032], and inside the range yesterday quoted (93.5% of quotes) the time-scaled smile is slightly better (+0.012 [+0.009, +0.016]; section 12).

## 12. Is the lead a wing effect? Two model-free benchmarks

The time-scaled smile repeats its edge value for a strike outside the range yesterday quoted. The linear-wing benchmark below continues the line through yesterday's 3 outermost quotes instead (added after the independent verification; only this one variant was tried; an SVI continuation is untested). Against the edge-value benchmark the jump model + misfit leads by -0.202; against the linear-wing benchmark by -0.045 [-0.061, -0.032] (ahead on 71% of days); the linear wings close 78% of the edge-value gap. Inside yesterday's quoted range (93.5% of quotes) the benchmark is slightly better than the model (+0.012); outside it (6.5%) the model wins (1.511 for the linear-wing benchmark and 2.288 for the edge-value benchmark against 1.100).

**Is the lead a wing effect? Next-day error (vol points) of two model-free benchmarks and the jump model + misfit, test period**

| Quotes | Share of quotes | Edge-value benchmark | Linear-wing benchmark | Jump model + misfit | Model minus edge-value benchmark | 95% interval (vs edge-value) | Model minus linear-wing benchmark | 95% interval (vs linear-wing) | Days model ahead of linear-wing benchmark |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all quotes | 100.0% | 1.236 | 1.078 | 1.034 | -0.202 | [-0.227, -0.181] | -0.045 | [-0.061, -0.032] | 71% |
| inside yesterday's quoted range | 93.5% | 1.006 | 1.006 | 1.018 | +0.012 | [+0.009, +0.016] | +0.012 | [+0.009, +0.016] | 52% |
| outside it | 6.5% | 2.288 | 1.511 | 1.100 | -1.189 | [-1.282, -1.106] | -0.411 | [-0.503, -0.338] | 81% |

*1173 test days, 524,959 quotes. Edge-value benchmark = the time-scaled smile (repeats its edge value beyond yesterday's quoted range); linear-wing benchmark = the same, but continuing the line through yesterday's 3 outermost quotes (floored at 2 vol points). Inside the range the two benchmarks are identical. The linear-wing benchmark was added after the independent verification; only this one variant was tried (results/benchmark_check/README.md).*

Figures: `figures/34_benchmark_inside_outside.png`.

## 13. Forecast variants: what the model's own dynamics add

hybrids.py stores seven forecasts per model; the main tables show two (model with today's state, and plus yesterday's misfit). For the jump model, the model's own one-day mean reversion changes the error by -0.002 [-0.006, +0.001], the leverage update by +0.090, leverage plus misfit is +0.102 worse than the misfit alone, and yesterday's smile plus the model-implied change is +0.084 worse than yesterday's smile. The forecasting value of the model is its state plus yesterday's misfit; for the jump model its own dynamics add nothing. For single Heston the variants are slightly better (mean reversion -0.016, leverage -0.038, leverage plus misfit -0.034 against the misfit alone, an interval that includes zero); for the diffusion model mean reversion changes the error by -0.006 and the leverage update makes it worse (+0.173).

| single Heston | yesterday's smile + model-implied change | 1.877 | 1.435 | yesterday's smile (no model) | -0.032 | [-0.068, +0.005] | 49% |

*Negative difference = the forecast in the row is better than the one it is compared with. Source: results/tables/forecast_variants.csv (exp_variants_table.py); the full table with the difference to the time-scaled smile is results/tables/forecast_variants.md.*


## How to reproduce

`python -m dh2.run_all --config configs/nifty.yaml` rebuilds every table, figure and number from the cached data (stages whose outputs exist are skipped; `--list` shows the cost of each); `--quick` is the demo-scale run in `results_quick/`. See `results/PIPELINE.md`.
